root_idea.summary: The root centers on the persistence or continuance of something.
root_idea.development: This orientation extends to remaining fixed, persistent illness or pain, sustained attention, perpetual punishment or obedience, and far-extending distance. These are related lexical developments, not interchangeable meanings of every derived form.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized singular active-participle citation form وَاصِبٌ.

senses.usage_conditions: In عَذَابٌ وَاصِبٌ, describes punishment that continues without cessation.

senses.definition: Continuously binding or obligatory, of obedience or religious duty.
senses.usage_conditions: In وَلَهُ الدِّينُ وَاصِبًا, describes obedience owed to God continuously, including when it is burdensome or not willingly accepted; the construction may therefore be understood as perpetual obedience or obligatory religion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To continue, remain constant, or stay fixed, settled, and firm.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a thing or condition; examples include milk continuing and fat remaining in an animal.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To persistently attend or apply oneself to a matter, and to manage or conduct it diligently.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction may describe a person, a group, or the sustained management of property or livestock.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become ill or suffer bodily pain; in some usages, to experience fatigue, weariness, or languor.
To suffer bodily pain or become languid.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A derived reflexive or inchoative usage referring to the subject's experience of pain or debility.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To tend, nurse, or take care of a sick person.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A causative/intensive caregiving construction used of attending someone during illness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cause illness or afflict someone with a disease, sickness, or malady.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction can also describe illness being brought upon children or upon a group's children.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a she-camel, to grow fat and remain so.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized animal-related construction describing a continuing state of fatness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a she-camel, to yield milk continually.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized animal-related construction concerning continuous milk production.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The space between the third finger and the first finger.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An anatomical noun referring to the interval between those fingers.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Disease, sickness, or pain; also persistent pain, bodily emaciation caused by fatigue or disease, excessive fatigue, weariness, or languor.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The listed descriptions are related manifestations of illness, pain, and debility; the plural is أَوْصَابٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Diseased, ill, sick, or in pain.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjective describing a person affected by illness or pain.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A very far-extending desert, seemingly without end.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival construction describing great or apparently limitless extent.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Afflicted with a disease, sickness, or malady.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive-participial description of one upon whom illness has been inflicted.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A she-camel that yields milk continually.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An animal-related participial construction describing continuous milk production.
An intensive passive-participial description of repeated or multiple afflictions.

lane_unit_coverage.note: The camel-milk example is covered by the continuing or constant sense.
The continuing fat example is covered by the general continuance sense.
Sustained attention to property or livestock is covered by the persistence construction.
The group's persistent application is covered by the same construction.
The divine affliction construction is covered by the causative illness sense.
The construction involving diseased children is explicitly covered by the causative illness sense.
Pointer-only cross-reference to the illness adjective.
The Quranic construction is explained both as perpetual obedience and as binding obedience despite difficulty or unwillingness.

cautions: The Quranic active participle وَاصِبٌ is kept distinct from the illness adjective وَصِبٌ and from the other derived forms.
A historical citation for the religion phrase is printed with an older surah reference convention; the example here uses the independently supplied QAC location 16:52.
